## Multivariable model

All candidates go in together. The variable with the largest P value is then removed, one at a time, until every remaining variable has P below 0.05. The paper gave no threshold for entry and kept no variable in by force. The model uses everyone with every candidate known, and the number left out is reported.

**Functions used:** [`backward_eliminate()`](functions.qmd#backward-elimination).

```{r}
#| label: models-multivariable
#| eval: false
```

## The paper's final model

The paper's eight-variable final model is also fitted exactly as published, on the same people as the backward elimination. Its odds ratios can then be compared with the published ones directly, whether or not the selection here keeps the same eight variables.

The two approaches answer different questions. Rerunning the selection asks whether the paper's method, applied to this data release, picks the same characteristics; selection by P value is unstable, so it may not, even when nothing is wrong. Refitting the published model asks whether the same characteristics have similar odds ratios here. The [Study design and methods](study_methods.qmd#outcome-and-analysis) page sets out these and the other choices in how the model is built.

```{r}
#| label: models-published
#| eval: false
```
